title: Migrate core/domain/value_objects/ hand-written ==/hashCode/toString classes to @freezed
rule: Naming/placement — "Domain/state models are immutable @freezed classes; never hand-write ==/hashCode for data classes"
why: Every non-enum class in this batch (Pin; ProgramStartingPosition; DelaySchedule/WeeklySchedule/RollingSchedule; ScopeLevel/ScopeValue/CurriculumScope; SefariaRef; StageOrder; StudyDayPattern — 10 classes across 7 files) hand-writes operator==/hashCode/toString rather than using @freezed, contrary to the stated codebase convention. All the ones I traced are currently correct, so this is not a live bug, but it is the exact pattern the standard calls out as risky: every future field addition to any of these classes requires manually keeping three methods in sync by hand with no compiler help, whereas @freezed generates all three from the field list and can't drift.
recommendation: Migrate these VOs to @freezed where the validating-factory pattern (private const constructor + public validating factory) fits, which all of these already structurally resemble; note any VO where freezed genuinely doesn't fit as a documented exception in coding-standards.md rather than leaving it a silent inconsistency.
acceptance_criteria: New or materially-changed value objects in core/domain/value_objects/ use @freezed, or coding-standards.md documents an explicit lightweight-VO exception.
No behavior change: existing equality/hashCode/toString tests for these 7 files continue passing unmodified after any migration.

corrections: Finding's own enumerated list totals 11 classes, not 10 (Pin, ProgramStartingPosition, DelaySchedule, WeeklySchedule, RollingSchedule, ScopeLevel, ScopeValue, CurriculumScope, SefariaRef, StageOrder, StudyDayPattern).
